cards.title: Finite Lean kernels of fifteen Atlas cards, with B56 repaired
cards.statement: Exact finite kernels of cards B2, B16, B31, B32, B48, B51, B57, B60, B61, B66, B68, B74, B85 and B90 compile in Lean/mathlib; B56 is replaced by the corrected statement that a regular codimension-one wall and a regular codimension-two coalescence locus in a two-real-parameter model cannot meet transversely, because the combined derivative is a linear map from R^2 to R^3 and cannot be surjective.
cards.assumptions: Finite real matrices and polynomial identities over the stated rings; two real parameters for B56; B90 is restricted to explicit local normal forms.
cards.failure_mode: The English card captions are stronger than the kernels. B56 makes no disjointness claim. The generic n=2 versus n=1 exponent statement of B90, measurements, continuum statements and physical readings are not certified.
cards.evidence_status: Lean source compiled on PR #21 with axiom audit, leanchecker and four mathematical false controls; GitHub Actions run 34684818137 succeeded at the pinned head. Not yet assigned an LC tag in the certificate registry.

cards.title: Bounded Collatz collapse certificate for 1 to 100000
cards.statement: For every natural number n with 1 <= n <= 100000 there exists k <= 400 such that the k-th ordinary Collatz iterate of n is 1. An executable bounded checker is connected to the trajectory statement by the soundness theorem reachesOneB_sound, and the finite range is discharged with native_decide.
cards.assumptions: Ordinary Collatz step; the stated finite range and step bound.
cards.failure_mode: Does not prove the global Collatz conjecture, a global contraction theorem, exclusion of nontrivial cycles or exclusion of divergent trajectories. Finite range only.
cards.evidence_status: Lean source merged to main (PR #40); dedicated Collatz workflow run 34724307086 and CI run 34724307093 succeeded at the merge commit. Registry tag CL-001 / LC-021.
cards.verification_scope: research/collatz/formal/CollatzBounded.lean at 82f1c4c03102a9dfee005314f4301a6d52db5485 under Lean 4.33.0 / mathlib v4.33.0. Related finite results LC-020 (prefix barriers, PR #24), LC-024 (one-cylinder exceptional threshold, PR #57) and LC-026 (collapse cylinder law, PR #66) are separate certificates and are not summed here.
cards.credit: Jeromie N. Beasley; the Collatz map and native_decide range checking are standard.
cards.next_step: Register LC-020, LC-024 and LC-026 as their own cards once the collatz project record exists; keep each finite statement separate.

cards.title: Finite Schur spectral-floor transfer and allocation floor for multi-plaquette SU(3) models
cards.statement: For the branch's finite original-link gauge models, a Schur spectral floor transfers to the retained block, and a nonuniform overlapping allocation gives a lower floor on the compared operator; the longest finite Lean chain recombines these with the PSD energy-resolved boundary bound.
cards.assumptions: Finite-dimensional Hermitian blocks with the stated positivity and overlap hypotheses; the branch's declared spatial models at the stated couplings.
cards.failure_mode: Finite-model lower certificates only. No volume-uniform moderate-coupling gap, no four-dimensional continuum construction, no Clay Yang-Mills statement.

cards.statement: The explicit block-triangular four-body wall is bridged by a positive-semidefinite null-vector argument that identifies the wall's normal eigenvalue with the stated finite kernel (B30 and B36 lineage).

cards.title: A continuous observable into a discrete codomain cannot change value
cards.needs_project: decide on inspection; lineage is the archived crossing-number question
cards.statement: A continuous map from a preconnected parameter space into a discrete space is constant; in particular a globally continuous natural-number crossing count cannot climb 0, 1, 2, ... without leaving the continuous/discrete hypotheses, for example at a wall, stratum or jump.
cards.assumptions: Preconnected domain; discrete codomain topology; continuity of the observable.
cards.failure_mode: The historical physical interpretation of the crossing-number question is not asserted; the theorem says where a count may step, not that it does.
cards.evidence_status: Lean source merged to main on 17 September 2026 by PR #65 (three theorems). The push-triggered main CI run 35248227416 failed at runner level after 3 seconds, so the certificate must be cited from PR #65's own workflow evidence, which was not inspected in this audit.
cards.credit: Jeromie N. Beasley; the underlying topological fact is standard (locally constant functions on connected spaces).
cards.next_step: Recover the PR #65 workflow run id and record it; rerun main CI.

cards.title: A closed capped corridor is a disconnection, not a distance
cards.statement: If breadth-first search over presentations of total relator length at most the cap exhausts its frontier from the start without reaching the target, and the target lies inside the cap, then the start and the target lie in different connected components of the length-capped move graph. For every official AC row the target has length 2 and every cap is at least 9, so every exhausted corridor is such a disconnection.
cards.assumptions: The move set and cancellation rule of the official verifier; the cap applied to total relator length; exhaustive enumeration of the start's component within the cap.
cards.failure_mode: Component size says nothing about whether the target is in that component, so a large corridor does not make a certificate likely. A cap proof excludes only paths inside the cap. The closed-set bottleneck method itself is not novel; the candidate contribution is the reproducible instance table on hard official rows.
cards.evidence_status: Exact finite computation with the official verifier: six pairwise-disjoint components and twelve closed corridors on the complete length-39 profile (15 September 2026). A target-outside Lean barrier theorem exists on PR #69 (draft); its numerical rows are release-gate pending.

cards.title: Exact capped exhaustion table for six hard Andrews-Curtis rows
cards.statement: For six official rows no record-length path stays within the stated total-length cap: ac-06969 (start 27, record 38) empty through cap 32; ac-00145 (15, 39) through 22; ac-06936 (25, 26/27) through 33; ac-03305 (24, 23/24) through 36, with the Stable path first at cap 37 and the AC path at cap 40 with 133M states; ac-03871 (23, 30/32) through 32; ac-05818 (25, 34/36) through 26.
cards.assumptions: Official move set and verifier; exhaustive capped search with the recorded state budgets.
cards.failure_mode: Each row excludes only paths inside its cap; the state budget (about 180M states in 15 GB) is the binding wall at the next cap, not a mathematical limit. Short rows held by few teams need humps of 10 or more letters above the start.

cards.title: Rank by the best length after two multiplications: the B31 reading as a beam key
cards.statement: Conjugations and inversions keep a presentation in its conjugacy class; multiplications cross to another class (card B31, Plate IV). Keying the beam by the best total length reachable after two multiplications with free rotations (P2), then by length, finds record-length paths that length-first keys prune at the hump.
cards.assumptions: The official move set; beam width and depth as recorded; the P2 lookahead computed with free rotations.
cards.failure_mode: A search heuristic, not a bound. No signal at records 46-60; P2 ties the best sibling on 62% of steps so plateaus are common; offline sibling-rank proxies for breaking the ties (Tests A and B of the ledger) and the trace-chain eye (B69/B79/B83) were negative; the Whitehead-minimal frame as a score was weaker than P2.
cards.evidence_status: Measured with pre-registered kill conditions: ties ac-03060 at 28 and sac-03060 at 30 on a one-team row (+1.0, submission 2638, 28 September 2026); record ties for ac-03305 and ac-01629 in A/B; negatives recorded at full size.
